headline: KSE-100 rebounds 1,422 points to 169,392 on record $21.4bn SBP reserves as Wall Street retreats and the 10-year Treasury hits its highest since 2007 ahead of today's FOMC verdict, now priced near 90% for a hike
mood: Fed decision day · hike odds near 90% the dominant swing factor

five_things.html: The KSE-100 gained 1,421.67 points (+0.85%) on Tuesday to close at 169,392.33, recovering most of Monday's Hormuz-driven rout. Breadth was strongly positive — 280 of 494 traded names advanced against 166 decliners and 48 unchanged — with UBL, FFC, LUCK, BAFL and PSEL collectively contributing roughly 640 points, while MEBL, JVDC and SAZEW dragged about 179 points off the index. The rally tracked the State Bank's FX reserves hitting an all-time high of $21.4bn on Eurobond inflows. Business Recorder and Daily Independent confirm the print.

Ahead of today's 2pm ET decision, CME FedWatch pricing has swung to roughly 87-90% odds of a 25bp hike — a sharp shift from the coin-flip odds priced just weeks ago — which would lift the fed funds target range from 3.50-3.75% to 3.75-4.00%. The move is being driven by hot inflation and a resilient jobs report. Yahoo Finance and FedRateCalc.

US equities softened into the decision: the S&P 500 fell 0.45% to 7,585.73, the Dow shed 0.63% to 52,093.11, and the Nasdaq dropped 0.78% to 25,981.57, as the 10-year Treasury yield briefly touched 5.04% intraday — its highest level since 2007 — before settling near 5.01%; the 2-year sits at 4.39%. CNBC and Yahoo Finance.

Brent rose to about $107.50/bbl, a four-month high, and WTI to $102.69, after Saudi Arabia reportedly cancelled export shipments following drone strikes that forced closure of its East-West pipeline, compounding the Hormuz-linked supply risk premium. Per Trading Economics and Fortune. A costlier import bill remains a direct headwind for Pakistan's current account.

Gold slipped roughly 1% to a six-week low near $4,270/oz, while silver eased to about $62.82, as a firmer dollar (DXY near 99.6) and the looming Fed decision pulled traders to the sidelines. Per USAGOLD and Yahoo Finance.

matrix.local_html: Tuesday's 0.85% PSX rebound to 169,392 was driven by the State Bank's FX reserves hitting a record $21.4bn on Eurobond proceeds — surpassing the December 2026 target of $20.2bn ahead of schedule, per Business Recorder. The SBP has held its policy rate at 11.5% even as August CPI ran hot at 11.15% y/y, per Trading Economics, well above the 5-7% target band. The rupee held broadly steady at 277.30 in the interbank market, per Business Recorder. Pakistan and the IMF are set to open talks around September 22 on the fourth EFF and third RSF reviews, alongside the country's first Article IV consultation in two years, with roughly $1.2bn in combined disbursement at stake per Pakistan Times and ProPakistani. Separately, the Finance Bill 2026 tax overhaul remains in its implementation phase, with the FBR's September 30 filing deadline for Tax Year 2026 approaching.
matrix.gcc_html: The Hormuz/Red Sea risk premium remains the region's dominant swing factor: Saudi Arabia's drone-damaged East-West pipeline stayed shut and reported shipment cancellations pushed Brent to a four-month high near $107.50. Against that backdrop, OPEC+ completed its rollback of voluntary output cuts, adding roughly 188,000 bpd in September before a planned Q4 pause. Non-oil momentum stays intact — the bloc's composite PMI held above 50 for a 21st straight month at 51.5, with Saudi Arabia's reading at 56.6 (25th month of growth) and the UAE's climbing to 54.2, its best in seven months, per MUFG Research. Riyadh's PIF continues executing its 2026-2030 strategy pivot toward commercial returns in logistics, mining and AI infrastructure ahead of the Saudi Mega Projects Summit (Sep 28-30), which is expected to showcase a pipeline exceeding $200bn.
matrix.global_html: Wall Street softened into Wednesday's FOMC decision, with the S&P 500, Dow and Nasdaq all lower Tuesday and the 10-year Treasury yield touching its highest level since 2007. CME FedWatch pricing now sits near 87-90% for a 25bp hike today — a marked shift from the near-even odds of just weeks ago, driven by hot inflation prints and a resilient labour market. On the policy front, Congress returned from recess with government funding secured through December 11 but no consensus on an AI regulatory framework, leaving lawmakers with only a handful of legislative days before the November 3 midterms, per Roll Call.

legislative.policy_html: IMF's 4th EFF/3rd RSF review and first Article IV consultation begin ~Sep 22, alongside the FBR's Sep 30 filing deadline under the Finance Bill 2026 tax overhaul
legislative.impact_html: Wins: banks and sovereign credit positioned for ~$1.2bn in combined IMF disbursement, reinforced by record $21.4bn reserves Loses: importers facing a wider bill from the Hormuz/Saudi oil shock; taxpayers facing the Sep 30 compliance crunch

legislative.policy_html: PIF's 2026-2030 strategy pivot continues alongside OPEC+'s completed output-cut rollback, ahead of the Saudi Mega Projects Summit (Sep 28-30)
legislative.impact_html: Wins: oil exporters capturing the Hormuz/pipeline-driven price premium; logistics, mining and AI-infrastructure allocations under PIF's re-weighting Loses: giga-project contractors facing scrutiny as PIF shifts toward commercial returns

legislative.policy_html: Today's FOMC decision, now priced near 87-90% for a hike, lands as Congress returns without an AI framework, funded through Dec 11
legislative.impact_html: Wins: AI incumbents facing no near-term federal guardrails; the dollar and short-end yields if the Fed hikes Loses: rate-sensitive growth stocks and long-duration bonds if the hike is confirmed

levels.support_note: Tuesday's intraday session low; deeper support at Monday's 167,971 close
levels.resistance_note: Tuesday's intraday high; then the 171,000 handle

desk_stance_html: We read Tuesday's bounce as relief buying on an idiosyncratic reserves headline rather than a durable trend reversal, given the hawkish global backdrop. Today's FOMC decision is the dominant swing factor — with a hike now priced near 90%, a confirmed move would tighten global dollar liquidity and pressure frontier-market flows just as the Hormuz/Saudi-pipeline oil premium keeps import costs elevated for Pakistan's current account. We would fade strength into the 169,988 resistance band and treat a close below 169,189 as confirmation that Tuesday's rally lacks follow-through. All levels are indicative desk estimates, not recommendations.

linkedin_text:
KSE-100 rebounds 1,422 points on record SBP reserves — but the real story today is the Fed, with hike odds surging past 85% and the 10-year Treasury at its highest since 2007.

THE OVERNIGHT TAPE
Wall Street softened into decision day: S&P 500 −0.45% to 7,585.73, Dow −0.63% to 52,093.11, Nasdaq −0.78% to 25,981.57. The 10-year Treasury yield briefly touched 5.04% intraday, its highest since 2007, before settling near 5.01%; the 2-year sits at 4.39%. CME FedWatch now prices roughly 87-90% odds of a 25bp hike at today's 2pm ET decision — a sharp swing from the coin-flip odds of just weeks ago, driven by hot inflation and a resilient jobs report.

PAKISTAN
The KSE-100 gained 1,421.67 points (+0.85%) on Tuesday to close at 169,392.33, recovering most of Monday's Hormuz-driven selloff. Breadth was strongly positive — 280 of 494 names advanced against 166 decliners — led by UBL, FFC, LUCK, BAFL and PSEL. The rally tracked the State Bank's FX reserves hitting an all-time high of $21.4bn on Eurobond inflows, already surpassing the December 2026 target. The rupee held steady at 277.30 interbank. SBP's policy rate stays at 11.5% despite August CPI at 11.15% y/y. Pakistan and the IMF open talks around September 22 on the fourth EFF and third RSF reviews plus the first Article IV consultation in two years, with roughly $1.2bn in combined disbursement at stake.

GCC
Brent rose to about $107.50/bbl, a four-month high, and WTI to $102.69, after Saudi Arabia reportedly cancelled export shipments following drone strikes that shut its East-West pipeline. OPEC+ completed its rollback of voluntary output cuts, adding ~188,000 bpd in September before a planned Q4 pause. Non-oil momentum holds — GCC composite PMI at 51.5 for a 21st straight month above 50, Saudi at 56.6, UAE at 54.2. Saudi's PIF continues its 2026-2030 strategy pivot toward commercial returns ahead of the September 28-30 Mega Projects Summit in Riyadh, expected to showcase a $200bn+ pipeline.

GLOBAL
Gold slipped about 1% to a six-week low near $4,270/oz and silver eased to roughly $62.82 as a firmer dollar and the looming Fed decision pulled traders to the sidelines. In Washington, Congress returned from recess with funding secured through December 11 but no consensus on AI regulation, leaving just a handful of legislative days before the November 3 midterms.

LEGISLATIVE TRACKER
• Pakistan: IMF's 4th EFF/3rd RSF review (~Sep 22) + FBR's Sep 30 filing deadline — wins for banks and sovereign credit on record reserves; loses for importers facing a wider oil bill.
• GCC: PIF's 2026-2030 strategy + OPEC+ cut rollback complete — wins for logistics/mining/AI allocations and oil exporters; loses for giga-project contractors under PIF's commercial-return pivot.
• Global: Fed's Sep 16 decision (hike priced ~87-90%) as Congress punts on AI rules — wins for AI incumbents facing no near-term guardrails; loses for rate-sensitive growth stocks and long-duration bonds if the hike is confirmed.

THE DAY AHEAD
KSE-100 support 169,189 (Tuesday's session low) · pivot 169,392 (Tuesday's close) · resistance 169,988 (Tuesday's intraday high). We'd fade strength into resistance and treat a close below support as confirmation Tuesday's rally lacks follow-through, especially if the Fed confirms a hike today. All levels are indicative desk estimates, not recommendations.
